parts.title: Teach & Review Concepts for Reading
teacherDirections: Read competition, notion, isolation, and illustrate first. Then teach the complete introductory 7.5 contraction sequence while keeping possessive nouns for subsequent lessons.

Show that a contraction combines two words and that the apostrophe represents the missing letter or letters. Include the irregular contractions don't and won't and the source groups formed with am, are, is, will, would, have, and had.

data.conceptNotes: A contraction is a shortened combination of two words. The apostrophe represents omitted letter(s). Contractions with not are taught first; don't and won't are irregular High Frequency Words. The source then extends contraction work to am, are, is, will, would, have, and had. Singular and plural possessives are subsequent 7.5 lessons and are not introduced in this first 7.5 lesson.
teachingMoves: Read competition, notion, isolation, and illustrate accurately before new instruction.
Build does not, then replace the missing o in not with an apostrophe to form doesn't; connect the two forms without changing meaning.
Build is not and form isn't the same way; then read can't, couldn't, didn't, hasn't, haven't, shouldn't, wasn't, weren't, and aren't while naming the two whole words.
Teach don't and won't as irregular contractions and High Frequency Words.
Extend the same apostrophe principle to the source contraction groups with am, are, is, will, would, have, and had; keep possessive nouns for a later 7.5 lesson.

interactiveSteps.teacherCue: Build does not, then form doesn't.
teacherDirections: Present does and not, then cover the o in not with the apostrophe card and read doesn't.
interactiveSteps.expectedStudentAction: Read does not and doesn't, then identify the missing o.
interactiveSteps.teachingPoint: The apostrophe in a contraction represents the missing letter or letters.

interactiveSteps.teacherCue: Use is not to form isn't.
teacherDirections: Present is not, replace the o with the apostrophe, and read isn't; keep the meaning unchanged.
interactiveSteps.expectedStudentAction: Read the two-word form and contraction, then name the omitted letter.
interactiveSteps.teachingPoint: Contractions shorten two words while preserving meaning.

interactiveSteps.teacherCue: Read the source n’t contraction family and name the two whole words.
teacherDirections: Read can't, couldn't, didn't, hasn't, haven't, shouldn't, wasn't, weren't, and aren't, identifying the two words represented.
interactiveSteps.expectedStudentAction: Read each contraction and name the two whole words.
interactiveSteps.teachingPoint: Most n’t contractions replace the o in not with an apostrophe; can’t removes n and o because can already ends in n.

interactiveSteps.teacherCue: Teach don't and won't as irregular contractions.
teacherDirections: Contrast do not with don't and will not with won't; read the High Frequency Word Cards.
interactiveSteps.expectedStudentAction: Read don't and won't and identify their two whole words.
interactiveSteps.teachingPoint: Don't and won't are irregular contractions and are memorized High Frequency Words.

interactiveSteps.teacherCue: Extend the apostrophe principle to the remaining introductory contraction groups.
teacherDirections: Read examples with am, are, is, will, would, have, and had, naming the two whole words and the omitted letters.
interactiveSteps.expectedStudentAction: Read each contraction, name the two whole words, and identify the apostrophe's job.
interactiveSteps.teachingPoint: Contractions are not limited to not; the same apostrophe principle applies to the source groups with am, are, is, will, would, have, and had.

In don’t, why is this contraction treated as irregular?

Read the eighth sentence with expression. Which word should receive emphasis?
In haven’t, what two whole words are represented?
Which words in the last sentence help explain why skating would be unsafe?

parts.title: Teach & Review Concepts for Spelling
teacherDirections: Spell competition, notion, isolation, and illustrate first. Then teach the listed 7.5 contractions by starting with the two whole words, identifying the omitted letter or letters, and placing the apostrophe where the letters were removed.

data.conceptNotes: For spelling contractions, identify the two whole words, determine the omitted letter(s), and place the apostrophe in the position of the missing letter(s). Keep possessive spelling for subsequent 7.5 lessons.
teachingMoves: Spell competition, notion, isolation, and illustrate accurately before new 7.5 spelling instruction.
Form doesn't from does not and isn't from is not, replacing the missing o with an apostrophe.
Spell can't, couldn't, hasn't, haven't, and shouldn't by naming the two whole words and identifying what is omitted.
Teach won't as an irregular contraction and contrast it with will not.
Use the Student Notebook contraction reference to reinforce that the apostrophe stands for omitted letter(s); keep possessive spelling for a later 7.5 lesson.

parts.title: Controlled Text Passage Reading
teacherDirections: Read The Clock that Couldn’t Tell Time, Part One, from Student Reader Seven printed p. 146. This is the first controlled 7.5 passage after the teacher-confirmed Sep 18 advancement from 7.4.

data.passageTitle: The Clock that Couldn’t Tell Time — Part One
data.passage:
The large grandfather clock sits against the wall next to the front entrance as usual. It’s been there for a long time and has been passed down time and time again to somebody in the Griffin family for over 200 years. The clock is stately with its maple panels, brass hands, and fancy glass doors. There’s just one problem - it doesn’t work!

The present-day owner of the clock, Conrad Griffin, thinks to himself, “What’s the use of having a grand clock if it can’t tell you the time?” He commits to find a way to fix this sad clock once and for all.
data.historyNote: 5A completed 7.4 with 15/15 charting for all three students on Sep 18 and was explicitly advanced to 7.5 for the next week. No 7.5 passage is recorded before this first 7.5 lesson.
